subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is a composite material?
options: A material made by combining two or more materials with different properties
A metal that has been heat-treated to increase its hardness
A polymer that changes shape when heated
A single pure element refined to remove impurities
questions.explain: A composite combines two or more materials so the result has improved properties compared with the individual materials.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a modern material?
options: A material developed through the invention of new or improved processes
A material that reverts to its original shape when cooled
A naturally occurring material used without any processing
A material that always decomposes within a few days
questions.explain: Modern materials are those created or made available through new or improved manufacturing and processing techniques.

questions.q: What defines a smart material?
options: Its properties change in response to a change in its environment
It is always made from two or more bonded layers
It is stronger than any equivalent metal
It can only be shaped by casting
questions.explain: A smart material responds to an external stimulus such as heat, light, pressure or electricity by changing one of its properties.

questions.q: Nitinol, a common shape memory alloy, is made mainly from which two metals?
questions.explain: Nitinol is a nickel-titanium alloy whose name comes from Nickel Titanium Naval Ordnance Laboratory.

questions.q: A thermochromic pigment changes colour in response to a change in what?
questions.explain: Thermochromic pigments alter their colour when the temperature rises or falls.

questions.q: A photochromic material changes colour in response to a change in what?
questions.explain: Photochromic materials darken or change colour when exposed to light, typically ultraviolet light.

questions.q: Glass reinforced plastic (GRP) is made from glass fibres combined with what?
questions.explain: GRP consists of glass fibres set within a polyester resin matrix, giving a strong, lightweight material.

questions.q: What is the reinforcing material in carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP)?
questions.explain: In CFRP, carbon fibres provide the strength and are held together by a polymer resin matrix.

questions.q: Graphene is best described as which of the following?
options: A single layer of carbon atoms
A blend of nickel and titanium
questions.explain: Graphene is a one-atom-thick layer of carbon that is extremely strong, light and electrically conductive.

questions.q: Why is titanium often chosen for aircraft parts and medical implants?
options: It has a high strength-to-weight ratio and resists corrosion
It is the cheapest metal available
It melts easily so is simple to cast
questions.explain: Titanium is strong, light and corrosion resistant, and its biocompatibility suits it to medical implants.

questions.q: Why can spectacle frames made from a shape memory alloy recover their shape after being bent?
options: Heat causes the alloy to return to its remembered shape
Light bleaches the alloy back to shape
Pressure permanently locks the new shape
questions.explain: Shape memory alloys return to a pre-set shape when heated, so warmth from the body or hands restores the frame.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of CFRP compared with steel for a bicycle frame?
options: It offers high strength with much lower weight
It is far cheaper to produce
questions.explain: CFRP provides a very high strength-to-weight ratio, making frames strong yet significantly lighter than steel.

questions.q: A kettle has a panel that changes colour as the water heats up. Which smart material achieves this?
questions.explain: Thermochromic pigments respond to temperature, so the panel changes colour as the water warms.

questions.q: Why is metal foam a useful modern material for lightweight structures?
options: Gas pockets make it light while it retains useful strength
It changes shape automatically when heated
questions.explain: Metal foam contains gas-filled pores that reduce weight while keeping a good strength-to-weight ratio.

questions.q: A composite is generally made from two parts. What are they?
options: A core and a laminate coating only
questions.explain: Composites combine a reinforcement (which gives strength) held within a matrix (which binds it together).

questions.q: What is the main environmental benefit of corn starch based polymers?
questions.explain: Corn starch polymers are made from a renewable source and can biodegrade, reducing plastic waste.

questions.q: A designer wants a baby's spoon to warn a parent when the food on it is too hot. Which smart material should be used in the spoon?
questions.explain: Thermochromic pigment changes colour at a set temperature, signalling when the food is too hot.

questions.q: A company needs a canoe hull that is strong, waterproof and lightweight at low cost. Which material is most suitable?
questions.explain: GRP is strong, waterproof, lightweight and relatively inexpensive, making it ideal for canoe and boat hulls.

questions.q: A floor tile is designed to generate a small electrical charge each time someone steps on it. Which smart material makes this possible?
questions.explain: Piezoelectric materials produce an electrical charge when mechanical pressure or stress is applied to them.

questions.q: A wound dressing needs to help prevent bacterial infection. Which modern material feature would achieve this?
options: Silver nanoparticles for their antibacterial properties
questions.explain: Silver nanoparticles are a nanomaterial with antibacterial properties, helping to keep a dressing sterile.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Design & Technology (1DT0) specification; Modern, Smart & Composite Materials
